subject: Follow-up: Dedicated pool — staged burst, isolation & SLA targets
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Rivera <lena@vectra.ai>, Vectra AI Procurement <procurement@vectra.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated pool — staged burst, isolation & SLA targets
Cc: 

Hi Lena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions.

Call summary (30m):
- Primary pain: unpredictable token-level costs and noisy latency spikes during peak batch jobs (model inference for annotator pipelines).
- Current infra: multi-tenant shared GPU cluster with spot instances; runs nightly retrains + daytime inference (real-time scoring for customer-facing features).
- Key goals: predictable throughput for 99th pct latency, tenant-level isolation for PHI workloads, capacity headroom for weekly burst jobs, and clear SLOs for billing/chargeback.

Redwood proposal (high level):
1) Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) sized for steady-state inference: ~4x A100-equivalent slots for 99% of traffic.
2) Staged burst window: additional reserved burst capacity (2x) that can be scheduled for nightly retrain and 3x/week peak runs.
3) Tenant isolation path: network segmentation + optional private pool (VPC) for PHI subset.
4) SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool, P99 token latency target to be validated in pilot.

Open items / asks from Vectra:
- Confirm steady-state RPS and typical sequence lengths (tokens) for scoring vs. retrain.
- Procurement contact and timeline for contract/PO.
- Any required compliance artifacts (SOC2 / audit window) we should include in the commercial package.

Attachments: I attached a short SLO draft and a proposed network segmentation diagram for your infra team to review (vectra-slo-draft.pdf, network-seg-diagram.png).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the RPS/tokens and procurement timeline (you mentioned procurement kickoff this week).
- If agree, we run a 2-week pilot: capacity sizing validation + isolation test (can be staged without full private deployment).
- Value checklist: estimate cost delta vs. shared cluster and verify throughput with 95/99 latency targets.

Would you be able to share estimated steady-state RPS and the procurement contact? I can loop in Ben (ops) and Jordan (solutions) to scope the pilot and draft an initial SOW.

Thanks,

--
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
https://redwood.inference

From: Lena Rivera <lena@vectra.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated pool — staged burst, isolation & SLA targets
Cc: Vectra AI Procurement <procurement@vectra.ai>

Camila — really helpful recap, thanks. Confirming a few points and adding procurement context.

Quick answers:
- Steady-state: ~120 RPS for inference requests during business hours, median sequence length ~180 tokens, tail to ~900 tokens for long-form customer reports.
- Nightly retrains: heavy batch jobs run 00:30–04:00 PST, 3–4 times per week, with spikes requiring ~3x steady-state for short windows.
- Procurement: procurement@vectra.ai is the contact. They typically need a 30–45 day window for PO and we use a standard vendor form (I attached a link to their vendor checklist below).

Questions from procurement:
1) Can Redwood provide a redlined MSA and an initial SOW for a pilot (2 weeks)?
2) Will we get access to billing breakdown per-tenant for chargeback during the pilot?
3) How do failovers and fallback to hosted variants affect SLAs / credits?

We reviewed the SLO draft quickly — looks reasonable. Procurement asked for a short appendix that shows data retention and audit log retention for the private pool.

If you can send the SOW + redline-friendly MSA and a short appendix on audit retention, I can share with procurement and schedule a procurement kickoff this week.

Thanks,
Lena
